results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Required] [Prerequisite]: Identify the exact target site/page/profile and disambiguate similarly named entities using COMPOSIO_SEARCH_WEB (add qualifiers like platform, region, and “official”).
[Required] [Prerequisite]: Run targeted discovery queries using COMPOSIO_SEARCH_WEB (traffic/visits/rank/popularity + period/region + “estimated”) and capture citations for traceability.
[Required] [Step]: Extract and shortlist credible source links from COMPOSIO_SEARCH_WEB using data.citations[*].id and/or data.citations[*].url (don’t rely on narrative text alone).
[Required] [Step]: Retrieve supporting passages from shortlisted sources using COMPOSIO_SEARCH_FETCH_URL_CONTENT (record metric, value, unit, period, region, plus methodology/definition text).

[Optional (if initial results are generic or missing figures)] [Next Step]: Refine queries and repeat the discover→fetch loop using COMPOSIO_SEARCH_WEB + COMPOSIO_SEARCH_FETCH_URL_CONTENT until concrete numbers and definitions appear.

[Optional (if you need a comparison table or conflict checks)] [Next Step]: Normalize extracted fields and flag discrepancies using COMPOSIO_SEARCH_VERCEL_AI_CHAT (standardize metric/value/unit/period/region/source).

[Fallback (if fetched pages are incomplete or key sections are cut off)] [Fallback]: Re-run COMPOSIO_SEARCH_FETCH_URL_CONTENT with a higher character limit or fetch additional relevant citation pages/sections discovered via COMPOSIO_SEARCH_WEB.
known_pitfalls: [COMPOSIO_SEARCH_WEB] Narrative summaries can omit or weaken traceability; citations are the reliable reference set for verification.
[COMPOSIO_SEARCH_WEB] Ambiguous queries can return citations for the wrong entity; filter citations to the exact intended identity before extracting metrics.
[COMPOSIO_SEARCH_WEB] Source links may be reliable only in data.citations[*].id (sometimes also .url); don’t assume a separate flat results list.
[COMPOSIO_SEARCH_FETCH_URL_CONTENT] Call can fail with a missing-field validation error if URLs aren’t passed in the required arguments shape.
[COMPOSIO_SEARCH_FETCH_URL_CONTENT] max_characters can truncate long pages (often ~30000–50000); key tables/definitions may require higher limits or multiple fetches.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Extract citation links from COMPOSIO_SEARCH_WEB output without assuming a flat results list.
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
def extract_urls(r):
    d=r.get('data',{})
    if isinstance(d,dict) and 'data' in d: d=d['data']
    c=d.get('citations',[]) if isinstance(d,dict) else []
    return [x.get('url') or x.get('id') for x in c if isinstance(x,dict) and (x.get('url') or x.get('id'))]
```

COMPOSIO_SEARCH_WEB.description: Perform a web search using the Exa API. Returns a nested structure: narrative summary under results.answer, sources under results.citations (and optionally results.organic_results). Prioritize results.citations as primary evidence over results.answer, which can be vague. Only indexes publicly available content — no paywalled, login-gated, or private content. No date filters enforced; include recency terms in query and verify dates in snippets manually. Throttle to ~1–2 requests/second; bursty queries trigger HTTP 429. Large responses may be stored remotely — use structure_info to locate results.answer and results.citations.

query.description: The search query for the Composio Exa API. Must be non-empty; using any other parameter name (e.g., 'q') causes an invalid-request error. Include qualifiers (year, region, platform, intent) for better results — broad queries return generic content; excessive site: or quoted-term filters can return zero results. Add disambiguating terms (city, role, domain) when searching for people or organizations with common names.

COMPOSIO_SEARCH_FETCH_URL_CONTENT.description: Fetch and extract clean, readable page text (markdown) from public web pages (HTML content) using the Exa API. Use when you need to retrieve actual content from search results or documentation links to extract setup steps, requirements, or citations. Only works with web page URLs - does not support direct links to images, PDFs, or other binary files.

text.description: Include extracted markdown text content from the page. Defaults to true.

urls.description: List of public URLs to web pages (HTML content) to fetch content from. URLs must be valid and publicly accessible. Do not use direct links to images (.jpg, .png, .gif), PDFs, or other binary files - use web page URLs only. Also accepts a single URL string.

extras.description: Additional content options like imageLinks or links counts (e.g., {'imageLinks': 3, 'links': 5}).

summary.description: Include AI-generated summary of the page content. Can be boolean or object with query/schema options.

max_characters.description: Maximum number of characters to extract from each page. Maps to text.maxCharacters in Exa API.
